sections.h2: Where do I find property records in Ellis County?
sections.html:
Ellis County land records are handled by the County Clerk's office at 109 S. Jackson St., 2nd Floor, Waxahachie, TX 75165. The same address is printed on the clerk's fee schedule for walk-in recording and for questions about copies.

  • Phone: 972-825-5070
  • Fax: 972-825-5075
  • Hours: weekdays, 8:00 to 4:30
  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 250, Waxahachie, Texas 75168
  • Make checks payable to: Ellis County Clerk

The county's website has moved to a new address, and older links to the recording pages now forward to the newer site. The Recording Division page lists eRecording through the county's approved vendors, which lets a title company or lender send documents without visiting the office.

One housekeeping rule shows up at the top of the fee schedule: every document must have a return address. Without one, the clerk has nowhere to send the file-stamped original after recording.

sections.h2: What does the Ellis County recording fee schedule say?
sections.html:
The schedule in effect since January 1, 2024 charges $25.00 for the first page of a document and $4.00 for each additional page, part of a page or rider. Names beyond the first five on one instrument cost $0.25 each.

Ellis County Clerk official public record fees, schedule effective 01/01/2024
ItemFee as printed
First page of a document$25.00
Each additional page, part of page or rider$4.00
Each name after the first five$0.25
Tax certificate$4.00
Federal tax lien or release$30.00
State tax lien, first page (filed by state agency)$15.00
State tax lien, first page (all others)$25.00
Plat or map, first page$70.00
Posting public notices$2.00

The sheet also prices plat pages after the first at $25.00 each, UCC financing statements at $35.00 or $50.00 when they run three pages or more, and hospital liens at $25.00. Veterans filing an assumed name certificate pay nothing.

A notice of sale for a foreclosure is posted at the $2.00 notice fee. Under the Texas county clerk manual, a notice has to appear at the courthouse and be filed with the clerk.

sections.h2: How do I pay and get copies at the Ellis County Clerk?
sections.html:
The clerk accepts checks made out to the Ellis County Clerk and charges a processing fee on cards. Card and debit transactions carry a 2.4 percent fee, with a $1 minimum. A returned check costs $25.00, and the office will not take a check more than 90 days old. Refunds wait until a check has cleared the bank.

Copy fees are modest and are set under Local Government Code Sec. 118.0145. A noncertified paper copy is $1.00 for each page or part of a page, and so is a paper document converted to electronic form. An electronic copy of an electronic document is $1.00 for a document up to 10 pages, then $0.10 for each page beyond that. A certification adds $5.00, and a full-size copy of a plat is $10.00 under Local Government Code Sec. 118.011.

Mailed documents go to the P.O. Box. A seller who needs a recorded copy quickly can a title company can pull it for you, since mail to a P.O. Box adds days.

sections.h2: How big and how fast-growing is Ellis County?
sections.html:
The land area of Ellis County is 935.75 square miles, and its population has climbed steeply this decade. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page shows 240,867 people as the July 2025 estimate, a gain of 25.2 percent over the 2020 base. The county counted 192,455 people in 2020 and 149,610 in 2010.

The 2020 count works out to 205.7 residents on each square mile, far below the more urban counties in the Dallas area. The housing stock reached 84,743 units in 2025, and builders took out 3,678 permits that year.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 75.8 percent for 2020 to 2024
  • Home value, middle of the owner-occupied range: $348,600
  • Median gross rent: $1,594
  • Households: 71,759, averaging 2.94 persons
  • Median household income: $99,595 in 2024 dollars
  • Average commute: 30.3 minutes

With three of every four households owning, most sellers here are selling the home they live in. Texas lists powers of attorney among the instruments the clerk records, which matters for an owner who must sign from another city.

sections.h2: How do appraisal and tax dates play into an Ellis County sale?
sections.html:
The appraisal district sets value each year as of January 1, then mails notices of appraised value for homesteads around April 1 and for other property around May 1, according to the Comptroller's calendar. The protest deadline is May 15, or the 30th day after delivery of the notice, whichever comes later.

The appraisal review board hears protests from mid-May, and the chief appraiser certifies the roll to taxing units by July 25. Units adopt rates by late September, and bills follow on or near October 1. A seller who is listing in spring should have the homestead notice in hand; it shows the value the buyer's lender will see.

  • Homestead appraisal cap: taxable value of a residence homestead may not rise more than 10 percent a year, measured from the prior year's appraised value plus new improvements.
  • Split payment: qualifying owners can pay half by November 30 and the rest by June 30 of the following year.
  • Delinquency: unpaid taxes become delinquent on February 1, with a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

Texas homeowners age 65 or older have a school tax ceiling, and the Comptroller says it can transfer to a new Texas homestead. That detail can affect a retiree's plan to sell and buy again, so ask the appraisal district about it before listing.

sections.h2: What should I confirm before I sell an Ellis County house?
sections.html:
Have the title company run a search of the deed history, any recorded liens and the current tax status. The clerk's index is the main source for the first two, and the county tax office is the source for the third.

  • Vesting deed. The grantee on the last recorded deed should match the seller. Texas lists general warranty, special warranty, quitclaim and trustee's deeds among the instruments recorded by the clerk.
  • Release of lien. A mortgage paid years ago can still appear in the index until a release is recorded.
  • Inherited property. If the owner died, the State Law Library says the heirs may need an executor's deed, a death-transfer deed or a court order, depending on how the estate was handled.
  • Unpaid tax. The lien dates from January 1 and follows the land, so delinquent years must be paid at or before closing.

The Comptroller says a school district must give a $140,000 homestead exemption and that tax bills usually go out near October 1. Ask the Ellis County tax office and the appraisal district whether the seller's exemptions are on file, and bring any over-65 or disabled veteran paperwork to the title company.

faqs.q: What does the Ellis County Clerk charge for a deed?
faqs.a: Under the January 2024 schedule, page one of a document is $25.00, and each later page, partial page or rider is $4.00. Each name past the first five on a document adds $0.25.

faqs.q: What are the Ellis County Clerk's office hours?
faqs.a: The clerk's fee schedule and Recording Division page both list weekday service from 8:00 until 4:30. The office is on the 2nd floor at 109 S. Jackson St. in Waxahachie, and callers dial 972-825-5070.

faqs.q: Does the Ellis County Clerk charge to use a credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. The fee schedule says a 2.4 percent processing fee, with a $1 minimum, applies to credit and debit card transactions. Checks must be payable to the Ellis County Clerk, and a returned check carries a $25.00 fee.

faqs.q: Can a title company e-record a deed in Ellis County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recording Division page says documents can be submitted through the county's approved eRecording vendors, so a title company or lender can file without going to Waxahachie.

faqs.q: What does a certified copy of an Ellis County record cost?
faqs.a: The clerk charges $1.00 for each page or part of a page on a noncertified paper copy and adds a $5.00 certification fee for a certified copy. An electronic copy of an electronic document costs $1.00 for up to 10 pages, then $0.10 per page beyond that.
